question: Who among the following is the author of the autobiography 'Lone Fox Dancing: My Autobiography'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ruskin Bond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lone Fox Dancing: My Autobiography" (2017) is the autobiography of the celebrated Indian author of British descent, Ruskin Bond. (रस्किन बॉन्ड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ruskin Bond lives in Landour, Mussoorie (Uttarakhand). His famous works include The Room on the Roof (which won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize), The Blue Umbrella, A Flight of Pigeons and Rusty stories.

• He received the Sahitya Akademi Award (1992), the Padma Shri (1999) and the Padma Bhushan (2014).

NOTE

• Famous autobiographies: Wings of Fire (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh), Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), Truth, Love and a Little Malice (Khushwant Singh).

question: In which of the following years did the battle of Plassey take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1757.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the English East India Company under Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal. (प्लासी का युद्ध — 1757)

• The Nawab was defeated mainly because of the treachery of his commander Mir Jafar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• After the battle, Mir Jafar was made the Nawab of Bengal, and the battle laid the foundation of British rule in India.

• Plassey (Palashi) is situated on the banks of the river Bhagirathi/Hooghly in West Bengal.

NOTE

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) — the Company under Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II; it was followed by the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), which gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

question: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma is associated with which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was a legendary exponent of the Kuchipudi classical dance, famous for his female impersonation roles, especially Satyabhama in the dance-drama "Bhama Kalapam". (कुचिपुड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, named after the village of Kuchipudi in the Krishna district; Siddhendra Yogi is regarded as its founder.

• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma received the Padma Shri (1970) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam — Kerala; Odissi — Odisha; Kathak — Uttar Pradesh; Manipuri — Manipur; Sattriya — Assam.

question: _________ was/were the mascot(s) of the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Juhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Juhi" was the official mascot of the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy 2023, held in Ranchi, Jharkhand. (जूही — शुभंकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India won the Women's Asian Champions Trophy 2023, defeating Japan 4-0 in the final at Ranchi.

• Hockey India organised the tournament at the Marang Gomke Jaipal Singh Munda Astroturf Hockey Stadium.

NOTE

• Famous sports mascots: Appu (elephant — 1982 Asian Games, Delhi), Sheera (tiger — 2010 Commonwealth Games, Delhi), Miraitowa (Tokyo 2020 Olympics), Phryge (Paris 2024 Olympics).

question: Sanchi stupa was rediscovered in the year ________ by General Henry Taylor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1818.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sanchi Stupa (Madhya Pradesh) was rediscovered in 1818 by General Henry Taylor, a British officer, after it had lain abandoned and covered by vegetation for centuries. (साँची स्तूप — 1818)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Great Stupa at Sanchi was originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka (Maurya dynasty) in the 3rd century BCE; its famous gateways (toranas) were added later under the Satavahanas.

• Sanchi is situated in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, near Bhopal, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1989).

NOTE

• A stupa is a hemispherical Buddhist structure containing relics. Other famous stupas: Amaravati (Andhra Pradesh), Bharhut (Madhya Pradesh), Dhamek (Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh).

question: In November 2023, who was appointed as the Chief Information Commissioner of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Heeralal Samariya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2023, Heeralal Samariya was appointed (and sworn in by President Droupadi Murmu) as the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) of India. He became the first person from the Dalit community to head the Central Information Commission. (हीरालाल सामरिया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Central Information Commission was constituted in 2005 under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005.

• The CIC is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee comprising the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

NOTE

• The RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 empowered the Central Government to prescribe the tenure and salary of Information Commissioners (tenure now 3 years). The first CIC of India was Wajahat Habibullah.

question: Stunted growth, which is common in children growing up in extreme poverty, is a sure sign of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Undernutrition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Stunted growth (low height-for-age) in children is a sure sign of undernutrition — chronic deficiency of energy, proteins and micronutrients in the diet. (अल्पपोषण / कुपोषण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Forms of child undernutrition: stunting (low height-for-age), wasting (low weight-for-height) and underweight (low weight-for-age).

• Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency) and marasmus (protein-energy deficiency) are severe forms of malnutrition in children.

• Government initiatives against malnutrition: POSHAN Abhiyan (National Nutrition Mission, 2018), Mid-Day Meal (PM POSHAN) and ICDS/Anganwadi services.

NOTE

• The Global Hunger Index uses undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality as its indicators.

question: Which Indian actress from the following, is also a popular dancer and received the Smita Patil Memorial award for her role in the movie Damini?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meenakshi Seshadri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Meenakshi Seshadri, an Indian actress and a trained classical dancer (Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi and Odissi), received the Smita Patil Memorial Award for her acclaimed role in the movie Damini (1993). (मीनाक्षी शेषाद्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Damini (1993), directed by Rajkumar Santoshi, dealt with a woman's fight for justice; Sunny Deol won a National Film Award (Special Jury) and Filmfare for the same film.

• The Smita Patil Memorial Award is given in memory of the celebrated actress Smita Patil, known for her contribution to parallel cinema.

NOTE

• Meenakshi Seshadri won the Miss India title in 1981 at the age of 17, one of the youngest ever winners.

question: In which of the following cities was the headquarters of Theosophical Society established in British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adyar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The international headquarters of the Theosophical Society was established at Adyar (Madras/Chennai) in 1882. (अड्यार — थियोसोफिकल सोसाइटी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Theosophical Society was founded in New York (USA) in 1875 by Madame H. P. Blavatsky and Colonel H. S. Olcott; they moved to India in 1879.

• Annie Besant became its president in 1907; she also founded the Central Hindu College at Banaras (1898), started the Home Rule League (1916) and became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (Calcutta session, 1917).

NOTE

• The society promoted the study of ancient religions and philosophy (Upanishads, Vedanta) and the ideas of universal brotherhood, karma and rebirth.

question: If the server manages to land a legal serve and the receiver is unable to return the ball, it is known as an ace and the server gets the point. Which of the following sport is referred here?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In tennis, an "ace" is a legal serve that the receiver fails to touch or return, winning the server the point directly. (टेनिस — 'ऐस')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tennis terms: love (0), deuce (40-40), advantage, fault, double fault, let, tie-break, volley, smash, lob.

• The four Grand Slam tournaments: Australian Open (hard court), French Open/Roland Garros (clay), Wimbledon (grass) and US Open (hard court).

NOTE

• Famous Indian tennis players: Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Sania Mirza, Rohan Bopanna, Sumit Nagal. Wrestling, boxing and shooting have no "serve", so the description fits only tennis.

question: At which of the following places is the Lalbagh Flower Show organised, where thousands of flower varieties are put on display in different forms with a particular theme (which changes every year) during the exhibition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengaluru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Lalbagh Flower Show is organised at the Lalbagh Botanical Garden in Bengaluru (Karnataka), twice a year — on Republic Day and Independence Day — with a new theme each time. (लालबाग पुष्प प्रदर्शनी — बेंगलुरु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lalbagh Botanical Garden was commissioned by Hyder Ali in 1760 and completed by his son Tipu Sultan.

• The garden houses the Glass House (modelled on London's Crystal Palace), where the flower show is held, and a famous rock formation (Lalbagh Rock) about 3,000 million years old.

NOTE

• Bengaluru is known as the "Garden City of India" and also the "Silicon Valley of India".

question: According to Census of India 2011, which is the largest religious community in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, Hindus form the largest religious community, constituting about 79.8% of the total population. (हिंदू — 79.8%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Religious composition (Census 2011): Hindus 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7%, Buddhists 0.7%, Jains 0.4%.

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India (7th after Independence); its motto was "Our Census, Our Future". The Census Commissioner was C. Chandramouli.

NOTE

• The first Census in India was conducted in 1872 (under Lord Mayo); a regular decennial (every 10 years) census began in 1881 (under Lord Ripon).

question: The Narora ________ Power Station is located in Uttar Pradesh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atomic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Narora Atomic Power Station (NAPS) is a nuclear power plant located at Narora, Bulandshahr district, Uttar Pradesh, on the banks of the Ganga. (नरोरा परमाणु विद्युत केंद्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Narora has two Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) of 220 MW each, operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).

• Major nuclear power stations in India: Tarapur (Maharashtra — the first, 1969), Rawatbhata (Rajasthan), Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu), Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu — largest), Kaiga (Karnataka), Kakrapar (Gujarat), Narora (UP).

NOTE

• India's nuclear programme is based on the three-stage plan of Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha, the father of India's nuclear programme; the Atomic Energy Commission was set up in 1948.

question: Which of the following Union Territories of India marks the lowest poverty in National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023 (released by NITI Aayog), among the Union Territories, Puducherry recorded the lowest proportion of multidimensionally poor population. (पुडुचेरी — न्यूनतम बहुआयामी गरीबी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The MPI measures deprivations across three equally weighted dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — using 12 indicators (e.g., nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, sanitation, housing, bank accounts).

• As per the 2023 review, about 13.5 crore Indians escaped multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21; Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya and UP showed high poverty levels, while Kerala, Goa and Delhi were among the lowest.

NOTE

• The National MPI is prepared by NITI Aayog with technical support from UNDP and OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative).

question: To which of the following classes of compounds does cyclohexane belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alicyclic compound.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂) is an alicyclic compound — a carbocyclic (ring) compound that behaves like an aliphatic (open-chain) compound and is not aromatic. (एलिसाइक्लिक यौगिक)

• It is a saturated ring of six carbon atoms with only single bonds (a cycloalkane).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Benzenoid aromatic compounds contain a benzene ring (e.g., benzene, toluene, naphthalene).

• Non-benzenoid aromatic compounds are aromatic but lack a benzene ring (e.g., tropolone, azulene).

• Heterocyclic compounds have at least one non-carbon atom (N, O, S) in the ring (e.g., pyridine, furan, thiophene).

NOTE

• Aromaticity requires a planar ring with delocalised π-electrons obeying Hückel's rule (4n + 2 π electrons). Cyclohexane has no π-electrons, hence it is non-aromatic (alicyclic).

question: Groundwater is an important source of water. The top level of the groundwater layer is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is water table.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The upper level/surface of the groundwater (the level below which the ground is saturated with water) is called the "water table". (भौम जल स्तर / वाटर टेबल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The water-saturated layer of rock/soil below the water table that yields water is called an aquifer.

• The process by which rainwater seeps down through the soil to recharge groundwater is called infiltration; deliberate recharging is rainwater harvesting.

• Over-extraction through tube wells and pumps causes depletion of the water table.

NOTE

• "Sea level" is the mean level of the ocean surface; a "well" is a man-made structure to draw groundwater — neither is the top level of groundwater itself.

question: Women's Reservation Bill 2023 [The Constitution (One Hundred Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023] was introduced in Lok Sabha on __________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 19 Sep 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Women's Reservation Bill 2023 — The Constitution (One Hundred Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023, named the "Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam" — was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 19 September 2023, the first day of business in the new Parliament building. (नारी शक्ति वंदन अधिनियम — 19 सितंबर 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Bill provides 33% (one-third) reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, including seats reserved for SCs/STs.

• It was passed by the Lok Sabha on 20 September and by the Rajya Sabha on 21 September 2023, and became the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.

• The reservation will come into effect after the first census and delimitation conducted after the Act's commencement, and will continue for 15 years.

NOTE

• It was introduced by Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal. Women already have reservation (at least one-third, many states 50%) in Panchayati Raj institutions under the 73rd/74th Amendments (1992).

question: Which of the following Parts of the Indian Constitution mentions about the relations between the Union and the States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part XI.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part XI of the Indian Constitution (Articles 245 to 263) deals with the relations between the Union and the States — both legislative relations (Articles 245–255) and administrative relations (Articles 256–263). (भाग XI — केंद्र-राज्य संबंध)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Financial relations between the Centre and the States are covered in Part XII (Articles 268–293).

• Part VIII — Union Territories; Part X — Scheduled and Tribal Areas; Part VII (dealing with Part B states) was repealed by the 7th Amendment, 1956.

• The Seventh Schedule distributes legislative subjects into the Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

NOTE

• Commissions on Centre–State relations: Sarkaria Commission (1983) and Punchhi Commission (2007).

question: Where of the following was Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s Home Rule Movement active?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded his Home Rule League in April 1916 at Belgaum (Poona session), and it was active in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar. (बाल गंगाधर तिलक — होम रूल लीग, महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Annie Besant started her own Home Rule League in September 1916 at Adyar (Madras), covering the rest of India.

• The movement demanded self-government (Home Rule) for India within the British Empire, on the lines of the Irish Home Rule movement.

• Tilak gave the famous slogan: "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it".

NOTE

• Tilak was called "Lokmanya"; he started the newspapers Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) and wrote "Gita Rahasya". Valentine Chirol called him the "Father of Indian Unrest".

question: When did Bindusara ascend the Maurya throne?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 297 BCE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, ascended the Maurya throne in 297 BCE and ruled up to about 273 BCE. (बिंदुसार — 297 ईसा पूर्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bindusara was known to the Greeks as "Amitrochates" (Sanskrit Amitraghata — "slayer of enemies").

• The Greek ambassador Deimachus was sent to his court by Antiochus I of Syria. Bindusara followed the Ajivika sect.

• He was succeeded by his son Ashoka the Great (c. 273/268 BCE), who fought the Kalinga War (261 BCE).

NOTE

• Maurya dynasty order: Chandragupta Maurya (321–297 BCE) → Bindusara (297–273 BCE) → Ashoka. The dynasty was founded with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

question: Which of the following is NOT a service of micro finance institution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Micro deposit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Microfinance institutions (MFIs) provide financial services to low-income households, chiefly micro loans (micro credit), micro savings and micro insurance. "Micro deposit" is not a standard service category of MFIs. (माइक्रो डिपॉज़िट — माइक्रोफाइनेंस सेवा नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Microfinance provides small collateral-free loans to the poor, self-help groups (SHGs) and micro-entrepreneurs who lack access to formal banking.

• The concept was popularised by Muhammad Yunus through the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh (Nobel Peace Prize, 2006).

• In India, the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme was started by NABARD (1992); the MUDRA scheme (2015) funds micro-enterprises (Shishu, Kishor, Tarun loans).

NOTE

• MFIs in India are regulated by the RBI (NBFC-MFIs). Small Finance Banks (e.g., Bandhan, Ujjivan) evolved from microfinance institutions.

question: Which Hindustani classical musician is credited with popularising the Sarangi as a solo classical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ram Narayan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Ram Narayan is credited with popularising the "Sarangi" — a bowed string instrument — as a solo classical instrument in Hindustani music, taking it beyond its traditional accompaniment role. (पंडित राम नारायण — सारंगी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2005); the sarangi is said to be the instrument closest to the human voice.

• Pandit Ravi Shankar — sitar maestro (Bharat Ratna, 1999); Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma — popularised the santoor; Pandit Jnan Prakash Ghosh — noted tabla player and harmonium exponent.

NOTE

• Instruments and maestros: Shehnai — Ustad Bismillah Khan; Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan; Flute — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia; Tabla — Ustad Zakir Hussain; Violin — Dr. N. Rajam.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for the promotion of international peace and security?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51 (a Directive Principle of State Policy) directs the State to promote international peace and security, maintain just and honourable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration. (अनुच्छेद 51 — अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 44 — Uniform Civil Code for citizens.

• Article 47 — duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and standard of living and to improve public health (prohibition of intoxicating drinks/drugs).

• Article 49 — protection of monuments, places and objects of national importance.

NOTE

• The Directive Principles (Part IV, Articles 36–51) are borrowed from the Irish Constitution; they are non-justiciable but fundamental in the governance of the country (Article 37).

question: The ‘Mangla’ oil field is located in which district of Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barmer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mangla" oil field is located in the Barmer district of Rajasthan. It was discovered in 2004 and is one of the largest onshore oil discoveries in India in recent decades. (मंगला तेल क्षेत्र — बाड़मेर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Mangla, Bhagyam and Aishwariya (MBA) fields of the Barmer basin are operated by Cairn Oil & Gas (Vedanta Ltd).

• Crude from Mangla is transported through a continuously heated pipeline (Barmer to Bhogat, Gujarat) — one of the world's longest heated pipelines.

• A major refinery-cum-petrochemical complex (HPCL Rajasthan Refinery) is coming up at Pachpadra, Barmer.

NOTE

• Other Indian oil fields: Digboi (Assam — oldest), Bombay High (offshore, Maharashtra), Ankleshwar & Kalol (Gujarat), Ravva (KG basin).

question: By what name is the species of Scaphopoda Mollusca 'Dentalium' commonly known?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tusk shells.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dentalium", a genus of the class Scaphopoda (phylum Mollusca), is commonly known as the "tusk shell" (or tooth shell) because its long, curved, tapering shell resembles a miniature elephant's tusk. (टस्क शेल — हाथीदांत जैसा कवच)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Scaphopods are marine molluscs that live buried in sand/mud and feed using thread-like tentacles called captacula.

• Classes of Mollusca: Gastropoda (snails), Bivalvia/Pelecypoda (clams, mussels), Cephalopoda ("head-foot" — octopus, squid), Scaphopoda (tusk shells), Polyplacophora (chitons).

NOTE

• Mollusca is the second-largest animal phylum; molluscs have a soft body, mantle and usually a calcareous shell. Pearls are produced by the bivalve Pinctada (pearl oyster).
